sentences.text:
2. Petitioner case is as Follows:
That on 24.05.2022 at about 07.00 PM., petitioner was riding motor cycle vehicle bearing Reg No.KA-40-X- 4088 in Kolar-Vijiyapura Road, Near Tippu Nagar,
Pujappa vs Reliance Gen Ins Co Ltd on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159326138/
1 Bangalore Rural District, wherein the driver of the Tractor bearing No.KA-06-TA-2131 drove it, with high speed, rash negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner motor cycle and caused the accident.
In the accident petitioner sustained grievous injuries, multiple fractures.

He was shifted to Shirdi Sai Hospital,
wherein he took first aid treatment, later he was shifted to MTB Hospital and he took treatment as an inpatient for the accidental injuries and he has spent Rs.5,00,000/-
for his medical expenses.
3. Petitioner stated that he is 53 years of age and he was farmer and was earning Rs.5,00,000/- per annum,

Further he stated that the accident occurred due the negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle and the jurisdictional police have registered Cr.No.068/2022 against the driver of the offending vehicle.

He alleged that the Respondent no.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle and he insured his vehicle with respondent no.1 and accident caused due to the sole negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle and as such both are liable to pay the compensation with interest and he prayer this tribunal to award the compensation amount by allowing the petition.
4. After filing of the petition, notice served to the respondents, respondent no.1 appeared through its counsel, filed the power and written statement by denying the petition averments in toto.
They contended that insured has violated the policy conditions and accident occurred due to the negligent act of the petitioner.
Respondent no.2 has not choose to contest the petition and he placed ex-party.
5. Petitioner examined himself as PW-1 and examined another two witness as PW.2 and PW3 produced and marked 18 documents which are at Ex.P.1 to 18 and they are fully cross examined.
Respondent No.1 got assessed the physical disability of the petitioner through the competent doctor of Victoria Hospital, Bangalore.
The report filed from the hospital is marked as Ex.C1.

The said assessment of physical disability is not disputed nor denied by the respondent No.1.
6.

Respondent no.1 has chosen to lead the evidence, there is no material on record to show that the respondent No.1 is prevented from appearing before this tribunal to lead his evidence hence respondent no.1 evidence is taken as nil.
7. I have heard the arguments from both the counsels appearing for both the sides and perused the entire records.

8. On the basis of pleadings, I have framed the following :
ISSUES 1.Whether the petitioner proves that on 24.05.2022 at about 07.00 PM., he was riding motor cycle vehicle bearing Reg No.KA-40-X-4088 on Kolar-Vijiyapura Road,
Near Tippu Nagar, Bangalore Rural District, wherein the driver of the Tractor bearing No.KA-06-TA- Pujappa vs Reliance Gen Ins Co Ltd on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159326138/
2 2131 drove it in a rash and negligent and caused the accident and thereby petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the said accident as alleged in the petition? .
2.Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation?

if so, what is the quantum and from whom?
3.What order or award?
Additional Issue no.1:
Whether respondent No.1 proves that the insured has violated the policy conditions and accident due to the negligent act of the driver of the two wheeler as contended in the written statement?

9. After carefully going through the evidence placed on record and taking into consideration of facts and attending circumstances of the case, my findings to the above issues are as follows;
Issue no.1: In partly affirmative Add.
Issue no.1: In partly affirmative Issue no.2: In partly affirmative Issue no.3:

As per final order for the following:
REASONS 10. Issue No.1, 2 and Addl Issue No.1 :- I have taken these issues together for common discussion so as to avoid the repetition of facts and reasoning.
PW.1 being the petitioner, he reiterated the petition averments in his examination-in-chief affidavit.

Petitioner stated that he took treatment in Sri Shiridi sai hospital, MTB orthopedic and truama Hospital, Manipal Hospital and Satya sai orthopedic and multi specialty hospital as an inpatient for 22 days.

entities.text: Satya sai orthopedic and multi specialty hospital
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: He has tender the police records, that is C/copy of FIR, complaint, IMV report, wound certificate, final report, 5 discharge summaries, which are at Ex.P.1, 2, 4 to 6 and 9, and reply notice is Ex.P.8.
According to the aforesaid document, it is true that the alleged accident is head on collusion between the two wheeler and the tractor.
11. On careful perusal of the aforesaid undisputed documents, it is evident that one Lokesha s/o Narayanappa was the driver of the offending vehicle.

Ex.P8 is the reply given by the owner of the offending vehicle where in he admitted that the Lokesh s/o Narayanappa was the driver of the offending vehicle as on the date, time, place of the accident and he has the valid DL and the insurance policy of the said vehicle is valid.
In the cross examination of PW-1, he admitted that he was carrying 15 Kg bag of fertilizer in the said two wheeler.
The aforesaid fact establishes that respondent has admitted his negligent act in the alleged accident.

Pujappa vs Reliance Gen Ins Co Ltd on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159326138/
3 12.

entities.text: Pujappa vs Reliance Gen Ins Co Ltd on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The final report filed by the investigating officer which is at Ex.P6, where in the jurisdictional police have registered the case against the driver of the offending vehicle involved in the accident.
Ex.P4 is the IMV report, it reveals that the two wheeler Bajaj Pulsar got damaged in the accident.
The aforesaid report establishes the involvement of the offending tractor and negligent act of the driver.

The final report which is at Ex.P6 is filed after investigation and it is the prima facie proof of the accident and the involvement of the offending vehicle and rash and negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Accordingly the police records cannot be doubted and disbelieved.

It is true that as per the complaint allegations, the informant Mohan son of the petitioner, stated that they have taken their injured father to hospital for treatment as such they could not lodge the complaint on the same day of the incident.
It is also true that the said delay is properly explained and mentioned in FIR which is at Ex.P.1.
There is no material on record to disbelieve the reason assigned for the unintentional delay in lodging the complaint.
13. Petitioner has tender the wound certificate, discharge summaries, inpatient record which are at Ex.P.5, 9 and 16.

the entry in the wound certificate reveals that petitioner has sustained fracture of right tibia and fibula, femur, commutted fracture of right calvilce with brachial plexus injury and they are all grievous in nature.
Ex.P9 is the (5) discharge summaries issued from Sri Shiridi sai hospital, MTB orthopedic and truama Hospital, Manipal Hospital and Satya sai orthopedic and multi specialty hospital.

The entry therein reveals that interlocking nailing of right leg femur, was done on 26.05.2022, plate and screw fixation of right clavicle bone and nerve transformation was done to petitioner by way of surgeries on 31.05.2022, 21.11.2022.
Further in total petitioner was inpatient for 22 in the aforesaid hospitals for the treatment of the accidental injuries.
Accordingly petitioner is entitled for the compensation under the following heads.

14. Pecuniary damages (Medical expenses) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization,
Medicines, Transportation, Nourishing food and miscellaneous expenditure:
Petitioner took treatment in Sri Shiridi sai hospital, MTB orthopedic and truama Hospital, Manipal Hospital and Satya sai orthopedic and multi specialty hospital.

entities.text: Satya sai orthopedic and multi specialty hospital
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Evidently worth nothing is elicited from the mouth of PW.1 to disbelieve the fact that he has sustained the injuries and multiple fractures in the alleged accident and he took treatment for the same.
Inasmuch inpatient report, discharge summary and the medical reports issued form the hospitals has to be accepted.
Admittedly petitioner has taken treatment and under went surgeries and he was in patent for 22 days in the hospitals.
Ex.P10 is the medical bills, which shows that petitioner has spent Rs.5,97,414/- for his medical treatement.
Further for attendant charges, transportation, nourishing food, he might have spend some more expenses.

Therefore in addition to the actula medical experiences I award Rs.60,000/- and hence, he is entitled for Rs.6,57,414/-
under this head.
Loss of income during laid up period.

Pujappa vs Reliance Gen Ins Co Ltd on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159326138/
4 15.

entities.text: Pujappa vs Reliance Gen Ins Co Ltd on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioner has not substantiated his nature of work and income as alleged in the petition.
Accident took place on 24.05.2022, however as per notional income chart, the notional income for the year 2022 is Rs.15,500/-, and same is assessed and considered as his monthly income.
Considering the accidental injuries and the treatment taken by the petitioner and the oral testimony of PW-3, I am of view that at-least 5 months he has lost his income.
Therefore I award Rs.15,500/- X 5 months = Rs.77,500/- as compensation under this head.
Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability.
16. The petitioner has examined the Dr.Krishna Prasad as PW-3.
He deposed that, petitioner has 43% of whole body disability.

Ex.C1 is the report of physical disability assessment of the petitioner issued from Victoria Hospital, wherein, after the physical examination of the petitioner by the competent doctor, he has assessed the physical disability of the petitioner as 70%.
Learned advocate for the respondent argued that the aforesaid assessment of physical disability is on higher side.
I have perused the evidence of PW-3 wound certificate, discharge summaries given from the hospitals, X-ray etc.
Evidently petitioner has not examined the doctors who have treated him in the hospitals.

It is true that petitioner sustained the grievous injuries and multiple fractures,
interlocking nailing of right leg femur, was done on 26.05.2022, plate and screw fixation of right clavicle bone and nerve transformation was done to him by way of surgeries on 31.05.2022,
21.11.2022.
Further doctor has deposed that 43% of physical disability is equal to amputation and it is dead weight in the body of the petitioner.
He deposed that after transformation of nerve it was not working properly, he deposed that no accuracy can be given for the said procedure.
He deposed that the effect of nerve transformation can be assessed only after 6 months.
According to PW-3 as there is no muscle movement in the right clavicle and it is termed as dead weight.
He deposed that the percentage of the physical disability will not be reduced even though the dead weight is removed.
He deposed the petitioner can do his daily work in his left hand only and not with the right hand.
It is true that petitioner has not tender any document to show that he is an agriculturist and he is having agriculture land.
Further it is also true that petitioner has lost his earning capacity and his future income due to the accidental injury which results in permanent disability.
It is true that petitioner has physical disability due to accidental injuries.
The percentage of loss of earning capacity due to accidental injuries is different from the percentage of physical disability due to accidental injuries.

Considering the medical reports, discharge summary and oral testimony of PW1 to 3, and Ex.C1, the whole body disability of the petitioner is assessed as 70% and functional disability as 100%.
17.
The monthly income of the petitioner is assessed as Rs.15,500/-, the age of petitioner as on the date of accident is 53 years as per the entry in Aadhar card which is at Ex P.12.

The multiplier applicable to this case is "11".
18.

It is true that petitioner has lost his future income, accordingly he is entitled for future prospectus as per the dictum laid by the Hon'ble Supreme court of India in Sidaram Vs Divisional Manager, United India Insurance Co.Ltd.

entities.text: Sidaram Vs Divisional Manager, United India Insurance Co.Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: And another reported in (2023)3 SCC 439 .

The said principle is also observed and applied by the Hon'ble High court of Karnataka in MFA Pujappa vs Reliance Gen Ins Co Ltd on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159326138/
5 No.100899/2024 order dated 19.06.2024.

entities.text: MFA Pujappa vs Reliance Gen Ins Co Ltd on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly petitioner is entitled for 10% future prospectus as he is 53 years of age and he is married and self employed.

Therefore the loss of income on account of permanent disability is calculated as follows;
Rs.15,500/-(Monthly income) + 10% future prospectus (15,500+1550)=17,050.00
monthly income is Rs.17,050/- X 12 (Months) X 11 (Multiplier) X 70% (Functional Disability) = Rs.15,75,420/-
Hence, the petitioner is entitle for Rs.15,75,420/- as compensation under this head.

Non-Pecuniary damages (General damages) (IV)Damages for pain and sufferings and loss of amenities:
19.
It is undisputed fact that petitioner has sustained grievous injury and multiple fractures.
During the hospitalization and rehabilitation period, he might have undergone lot of pain and sufferings and due to accidental injuries.
There fore I award Rs.40,000/- under these conventional heads.

V) Loss of Amenities :-
20.
The petitioner has to forego certain amenities available for him due to the accidental injuries.
Therefore I award Rs.40,000/- as compensation under this head.
According to PW-3, petitioner can opt for removing the dead weight and he can have the cosmetic hand.
Petitioner has not whispered anything in respect of aforesaid fact.
21. Except these heads the petitioner is not entitled for compensation under any other heads.

In all the petitioner is entitled for compensation as follows:
 Sl No.
Particulars

Amount  1 Towards attendant charges, Rs. 6,57,414/-
 transportation, nourishing food  2 Loss of income during the laid up Rs. 77,500/-
 period  3 Loss of income on account of Rs.15,75,420/-
 permanent disability and future  prospectus  4 pain & sufferings Rs. 40,000/-
 5 loss of amenities Rs. 40,000/-
 TOTAL Rs.23,90,334/-
22.
Rate of Interest:
The Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, in Sarala Verma and others V/s
Delhi Transport corporation reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, wherein it is held that it is just and proper to award interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
Accordingly I award the interest at the rate of 6% P.A on the compensation amount form the date of filing of the petition till its realization.

6 23.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Liability:
The insurance company has not disputed the validity of the policy of the offending vehicle.
In the cross examination of PW-1, he admitted that he was carrying 15 Kgs of fertilizer in Bajaj pulsar.
The said fact corroborates with the facts stated in the complaint which is at Ex.P.2.
Counsel appearing for respondent NO.1, argued that in two wheeler only two persons are allowed, and they are not allowed to carry any luggage in the two wheeler.

Further argued that due to the said luggage,
petitioner has lost his control over the vehicle and he has contributed his negligence for the alleged accident.
Accordingly considering the facts and attending circumstance, based on the evidence the petitioner negligence is assessed as 15%.

Accordingly the respondent No.1 is the liable to pay 85% of the compensation amount that is Rs.20,31,784/- and respondent No.1 is directed to deposit aforesaid percentage of compensation amount with interest before this Tribunal within one month from the date of this order.

Hence with the aforesaid discussion based on the evidence placed on record, Accordingly I am answering Issue No.1, 2 and additional issue No.1 in partly affirmative.
24. Issue No.3:
For the foregoing reason and discussion, on point No.1, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER The petition filed by the petitioner U/s.166 of Motor vehicle Act,1988, is partly allowed with cost.
Petitioner is entitled for the compensation amount of Rs.20,31,784/- with interest at the rate of 6% P.A from the date of filing of the petition till its realization.
Respondent no.1 is directed to deposit the compensation amount with interest before this tribunal with in 30 days from the date of the judgment.

After depositing the compensation amount with interest, petitioner is permitted to withdraw 85% of the compensation amount with interest through K2, after compliance of mandate of circular No.39/2020 dated 17.01.2020.
Cash shirestedhar is directed to deposited 15% of the compensaton amount of the petitioner in any nationalized bank for a period of 3 years.
Advocate fee of Rs.1000/- is fixed.
All the interim applications pending if any stands disposed of.
Draw award accordingly.

ORDER The petition filed by the petitioner U/s.166 of Motor vehicle Act,1988, is partly allowed with cost.
Petitioner is entitled for the compensation amount of Rs.20,31,784/- with interest at the rate of 6% P.A from the date of filing of the petition till its realization.
Respondent no.1 is directed to deposit the compensation amount with interest before this tribunal with in 30 days from the date of the judgment.

After depositing the compensation amount with interest, petitioner is permitted to withdraw 85% of the compensation amount with interest through K2, after compliance of mandate of circular No.39/2020 dated 17.01.2020.
Cash shirestedhar is directed to deposited 15% of the compensaton amount of the petitioner in any nationalized bank for a period of 3 years.
Advocate fee of Rs.1000/- is fixed.
All the interim applications pending if any stands disposed of.
